blocks.h2: Signs Your Geneva Water Heater Needs Repair
blocks.intro: Most calls start with one of these:

tiles.body: A worn thermocouple or flame sensor, usually a straightforward repair.
A failing element or burner, a broken dip tube or a heater too small for the household.
A drain valve or relief valve leak is fixable. A leak from the tank isn't.
Usually the anode rod reacting with the water. A different rod often fixes it.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Problems in Geneva Homes
blocks.intro: Geneva's homes span almost two centuries, and the water heater setup varies with them.

items.body: Older basements can have low ceilings, narrow stairs and odd corners. Repairs and replacements take planning, and we measure before we quote.
Gas heaters in older homes often vent into a masonry chimney. If the furnace was upgraded and vents out the wall, the water heater may not draft well alone. We check it on every gas heater.
More than 4 in 10 Geneva homes were built after 1990. If one of them still has its original heater, it's likely past its expected life.
Geneva's reverse osmosis plant lowered the hardness of city water. Less scale is good for heaters, but any heater that's been in service since before then may still carry old sediment.

bodies: We service every type of residential water heater in Geneva: gas and electric tanks, power-vent and high-efficiency units and tankless heaters. Diagnosis first, recommendation second.

When you call, read us the label on the tank. The fuel, the size and the manufacture date tell us a lot before we arrive. If it's time to replace it, see [water heater installation](/geneva/water-heater-installation).

A yearly flush clears whatever sediment has collected at the bottom of the tank, keeps the heater efficient and helps it last. We also test the relief valve, check the anode rod and look over the burner or elements and the vent.
Tankless units get descaled on a schedule. If your heater has never had any maintenance, this is a good place to start.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Questions From Geneva Homeowners

items.q: Why does my hot water smell like rotten eggs?
items.preview: Usually the anode rod reacting with the water.
items.answer: Usually it's a reaction between the anode rod in the tank and the water. Replacing the rod with a different type often fixes it. If the smell is in the cold water too, the source is elsewhere.

items.q: Is my water heater worth repairing?
items.preview: Under about 8 years, usually yes. Over 12, usually no.
items.answer: If it's under about 8 years old and a part failed, a repair usually makes sense. Past 12 years, or if the tank leaks, replacing it is the better value.

items.q: How long do water heaters last in Geneva?
items.answer: Tank heaters usually last somewhere around 8 to 12 years. Yearly flushing helps them reach the longer end.

items.q: Do you service water heaters in older homes near downtown?
items.preview: Yes. We plan around tight basements.
items.answer: Yes. Historic basements can be tight, with low ceilings and narrow stairs. We plan the work and measure before we quote.

items.q: How much does water heater repair cost in Geneva?
items.preview: It depends on the part and the heater. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what failed and the type of heater. We diagnose it and you approve a flat-rate price before we start.
